courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identi: Courier Relay protocol-1 delivery identity (source: vendor/protocol-1.md): delivery_id ALONE identifies a delivery across ALL accounts, not per-account. Two receipts with the same delivery_id but different account_id are duplicates of the same delivery identity, not separate identities -- account attribution never changes this. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery_id: the one with the earliest occurred_at UTC instant (compare as UTC, converting any explicit numeric offset); ties broken by smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts sharing that delivery_id are duplicates. This applies to any command that groups/accepts/dedupes receipts under protocol 1 (e.g. count, and future commands that list or return accepted receipts), even when a given request happens to be scoped to one account_id.
courier-relay/protocol-2-current-and-del: Courier Relay protocol-2 delivery identity and current-protocol adoption (source: trial-kg1 issue text, approved by integration owner csells): the provider permanently adopted protocol 2 as the current agreement -- an omitted "protocol" field now selects "2" (was "1"). Identity is the pair (account_id, delivery_id): the same delivery_id under a different account_id is now a SEPARATE delivery identity (unlike protocol 1, where delivery_id alone identified a delivery across all accounts). Exactly one receipt is accepted per (account_id, delivery_id) identity: the one with the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant (opposite of protocol 1's earliest-wins); ties broken by smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts sharing that identity are duplicates. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when explicit numeric offsets cross a date boundary. Each accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload; accepted receipts are presented in original input order (not currently surfaced by count/summary, whose shapes are unchanged: protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count -- relevant if a future command returns the receipt list). Explicit protocol "1" continues to use the original protocol-1 contract (see courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity) unchanged and remains supported indefinitely. This identity contract comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee. Applies to any command that groups/accepts/dedupes receipts (count, summary, and future such commands), for the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates.
